title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 352 (Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account)

content.overview: Where a company is being wound up and the liquidator has money representing (a) dividends payable to any creditor unpaid for six months after declaration, or (b) assets refundable to any contributory undistributed for six months after becoming refundable, the liquidator shall forthwith deposit that money into a separate special account known as the Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account maintained in a scheduled bank. On dissolution, unpaid dividends and undistributed assets still in hand must also be paid into that account. The liquidator furnishes a prescribed statement to the Registrar. Claimants may apply to the Registrar for payment; unclaimed money after fifteen years is transferred to the general revenue account of the Central Government (subject to later claim). Retention in breach attracts 12% interest, penalty, expense liability and, in Tribunal winding up, possible remuneration disallowance or removal.
content.glance: Unpaid dividends (6 months) and undistributed assets (6 months) must be deposited into the Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account; 15-year unclaimed money goes to general revenue; breach attracts interest and sanctions.
content.study: Section 352 creates a statutory holding account for stale dividends and undistributed assets. After six months of non-payment of declared dividends or non-distribution of refundable assets, the liquidator must deposit the money into the Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account at a scheduled bank and furnish a prescribed statement to the Registrar. The same duty applies on dissolution for sums still in hand. Claimants apply to the Registrar, who must settle within sixty days or report to the Regional Director. Money remaining unclaimed for fifteen years is transferred to the Central Government’s general revenue account, but claims may still be preferred. Breach of the deposit duty attracts interest at twelve per cent, penalty, expense liability and, in Tribunal winding up, possible disallowance of remuneration or removal.

sections.body: Claimants apply to Registrar; after 15 years unclaimed money transfers to general revenue (subject to later claim).

provisions.title: Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account

examples.title: Stale dividend
examples.body: A dividend declared to a creditor remains unpaid for eight months. The liquidator must deposit it into the Company Liquidation Dividend and Undistributed Assets Account under s. 352.

hypotheticals.question: Can a claimant recover after the 15-year transfer to general revenue?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. Sub-section (7) allows a claim to be preferred under sub-section (6) as if the transfer had not been made.

misconceptions.trap: Unpaid dividends may remain with the liquidator indefinitely.
misconceptions.correction: After six months they must be deposited into the special account; after fifteen years unclaimed money goes to general revenue.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. State the rule of s. 352. II. Apply to facts. III. Conclude.
